NAVAJO N 
 
NAVAJO COUNTY 
 
               COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DEPARTMENT 
 
 
STAFF REPORT  
 
 
TO:    Planning and Zoning Commission 
 
FROM:   Berrin Nejad, Community Development Director 
  
THROUGH:    John Osgood, Public Works Director 
 
HEARING DATE:  June 4, 2020 - Special Meeting   
 
PROJECT NUMBER: Case #19-100 - High Pines - Zone Change with  
    Master Development Site Plan – CONTINUATION  
 
This item was heard by the Navajo County-Planning and Zoning Commission during the November 
21, 2019 meeting.  After presentations and discussions, it was decided that the project needed more 
work, based on the questions raised in the meeting.  At the end of discussions, the applicant was asked  
Whether he wanted to withdraw or table the item. H e chose to “withdraw,” but his intention to table 
the item in order to do more work on the project and come back to commission on a later date.   After 
the meeting, the applicant and his team had several meetings with staff and worked on the issues raised 
in the meeting such as revising the site plan and providing other documents that were missing in the 
earlier meeting.  This item is technically a “continuation”of the item from November 21, 2019 
meeting.  
 
BACKGROUND:  
The applicant is seeking a zone change approval with a master development site plan on both 
properties, from the current R1-43 zone that requires 1-acre minimum lots to SD-Special Development 
zone to gain more flexibility and allow for smaller lots.   
 
LEGAL DESCRIPTION:  The project was published with the following legal ad for both November 
21, 2019 and the June 4, 2020 meeting.  
 
CASE # 19 -100 ZONE CHANGE, DISTRICT IV:  Discussion and possible action on a 
request by Travis Barney for a Zone Change from ex isting R1-43 zoning on two parcels 
totaling 93.60 acres to Special Development on APN 208 -03-002A & 002B, a portion of 
Township 11 North, Range 18 East, Section 3 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian in the 
Aripine area. (Continue from November 19, 2019)

<!-- page 671 -->
Planning and Zoning Commission                                     June 4, 2020 - Special Meeting        2 | P a g e  
NOVEMBER 21, 2019- P&Z COMMISSION MEETING: 
 
The Commission reviewed the proposal with staff report, maps, and other attachments with 
presentations from staff, the applicant, and the applicant’s engineer.  (Attachment 4-Staff Report) 
 
During the discussions, the following items were introduced by the commissioners.  (Attachment 3-
Minutes of November 21, 2019).   Staff has reviewed the meeting minutes and listed each concerning point 
raised by the commissioners in the meeting and attempted to summarize with applicant’s responses.  
The applicant and his engineer will be presenting the project, the changes, and the issues listed below 
in detail during the June 4, 2020 meeting.  
 
The following is a summary of the issues raised in the November meeting: 
  
1- Master Development Site Plan- Lack of Open Space or amenities.  
The site layout was created 15 years ago with 50 lots.  With the new proposal, applicant is 
requesting 100 lots, thus, lot sizes and locations have changed but the roadways remained the same.    
After meetings with staff, a bubble format site plan is provided for zone change approval with the 
intention of bringing detailed lot layout plan in Tentative Plat stage.   
 
After the November meeting, the applicant worked with his engineer on the site plan  and made 
some changes.  (Attachment 1- New Site Plan).  The new site plan now has 9.42 acres of open 
space which did not exists in the previous plan.  The open space is created on the western side of 
the property, along the wash.  There is also a trail system, coming from Forest Services land, going 
through property, connecting East and West, and then going to the Forest Service land on the East 
side of the property.   This trail is for walking hiking, horses, etc. and open to the public. 
 
Creating the open space resolved several concerns brought up in the November meeting such 
as wildlife corridor, Day Wash, and flood concerns. 
 
2- Arizona Game and Fish 
No fences will be in open space to prevent injury to the wildlife and this open space will functio n 
as a corridor for wildlife.  
 
3- Waste Management  
The dumpsters will have covers and maybe fencing around it.  This will be included and enforced 
by the CC&R’s. 
 
4- Flood Control 
By creating open space and adding this area to the lots, ownership will go to the property owner(s).   
The resident(s) will own this area as part of their property and no structure or fence will be allowed 
to be built.    
 
5- Water Plans: 
The Water Improvement Plans were created in 2006.  The applicant would like to update this study 
after the zone change approval  which will include several percolation tests on the property  by 
meeting the ADEQ requirements.  The results will determine the lot layout that will be reflected 
on the Tentative Plat. (Attachment 8)

<!-- page 672 -->
Planning and Zoning Commission                                     June 4, 2020 - Special Meeting        3 | P a g e  
6- Day Wash 
Adopting Arizona Game and Fish recommendation and keeping it as open space. 
 
7- Concerns of Nitrogen Overloading: 
The 100 requested units are the maximum number which will be determined later with the 
percolation test results and how buildable the site will be.  In some cases, lots maybe combined 
due to topography or any other natural difficulties of the land which will reduce the number of 
units with bigger lots.  The septic calculations will be determined by the ADEQ requirements.   
 
8- Roads paved: 
The internal roads will be paved to County standards and will be dedicated to the County later.  
 
9- Density Concerns: 
The new site plan is bubble diagram format and does not depict lots. The sizes and locations are 
not determined yet. 
 
10- Phasing: 
The project will proceed in two phases:  Phase 1:  Southern portion and closer to the highway, and 
then Phase 2 in northern portion.  
 
11- Well to be Drilled: 
There will be a well and tank on the property, shown in blue on the site plan.  It is located in 
northern portion, which is Phase 2, but water campus will be built in Phase 1. (See Water Campus 
Plans, page C-2).  
 
12- Building homes or selling lots:  
The applicant will build the houses and then sell them.  
 
13-  On-site Drainage:  
The new design will allow water to go directly to the wash.  
 
14- Whether the lots are buildable: 
The applicant will have to make adjustment to lot configurations. 
 
15- ADOT approval was not current: 
ADOT approval is 15 years old.  The applicant wants to get the rezoning approval then apply for 
an ingress/egress permit.  If a permit is not granted  by ADOT, the project cannot move forward. 
(Attachment 7) 
 
16- Perimeter fencing: 
There will be no fencing. 
  
17- Travel Management Rules for Forest Service roads. 
The engineer stated that FS 332 is not on Forrest Service Road Closure plans and Navajo County 
has the easement.  Therefore, 332 will not be closed.  
 
18- If the Fire Chief was consulted. 
Chief McCluskey previously provided a letter and spoke in November meeting. (Attachment 6)

<!-- page 673 -->
Planning and Zoning Commission                                     June 4, 2020 - Special Meeting        4 | P a g e  
The following sections-Finding of Facts and Staff Recommendations- are from the November 
meeting and provided to Commissioners for reference in this evening’s hearing.  
 
From November 21, 2019- STAFF REPORT: 
 
FINDINGS OF FACT: 
 
1. The item has been properly noticed and posted in compliance with Arizona Revised Statutes and 
Article 29. 
Postcards were sent for this item to neighbors within 300 feet on Tuesday, November 6 th, 2019.  The 
physical properties were posted, and legal notice was posted within The Holbrook Tribune on 
Wednesday, November 7th, 2019. 
 
The property has been properly posted and neighbors notified for the June 4, 2020 meeting.  Staff 
received one phone call to find out if this was any different than previous project. 
 
2. The change is NOT in compliance with the Comprehensive Plan. 
While this proposed Zone Change and Master Development Plan meet a number of goals in the Navajo 
County Comprehensive Plan, they do not meet many goals and policies that can be readily be achieved 
due to the applicant’s decision to proceed with their proposal as submitted. 
 
The applicant made changes to the site plan to reflect the improvements in the new submittal.  
 
3. The change will NOT have minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and general 
welfare of properties in the vicinity of the proposed use. 
There are concerns with this proposed Zone Change as submitted as far as the public health and safety 
of those who would live within it as well as those who would interact with it on the nearby State Route 
260. 
 
The applicant re-submitted a new site plan to reflect the improvements to the development. 
 
 
 
STAFF RECOMMENDATION:  (from November meeting)  
Planning and Zoning Staff recommends that the Planning and Zoning Commission make the 
recommendation of denial of the Master Development Plan and Zone Change to Special Development 
Zoning to the Navajo County Board of Supervisors due to the following: 
 
1. This proposal, as submitted, does not comply with the Comprehensive Plan and will not have 
 minimal adverse effects on the public health, safety, and welfare of those nearby.  
 
 2.  The applicant has not provided any open space to allow them to deviate from design standards 
   or increase the development density, which has been requested with this Zone Change. 
 
3. Floodway and floodplain have not been dedicated as a tract, which is ne cessary for public 
 safety. 
 
4. The provided plan only provides for one usage type, single -family residential, which does not 
 align with the purpose of the Special Development zone.

<!-- page 674 -->
Planning and Zoning Commission                                     June 4, 2020 - Special Meeting        5 | P a g e  
 
5. No development standards outside of setbacks have been provided. 
 
6. No proposed structures have been shown in plans as far as location on parcels.  Additionally, 
 there have been no elevations provided to indicate architectural type and construction 
 standards. 
 
As noted throughout this report, applicant has considered the findings of facts and staff 
recommendations listed above and has made progress in addressing those issues. 
 
 
FOR THE JUNE 4, 2020 MEETING:  
   
After hearing applicant and engineer’s presentation and reviewing the provided documents, the 
Commission will draw their conclusion according the Finding of Facts listed in the staff report above.  
  
If the Planning and Zoning Commission concludes to make an approval recommendation to the Navajo 
County Board of Supervisors for the Case #19-100 - High Pines, Master Development Plan and Zone 
Change to Special Development Zoning, staff recommends additional stipulations stated with the 
motion:  
 
RECOMMENDED STIPULATIONS (if recommendation is approval):  
 
1. The lot configurations shall be detailed in Tentative Plat with lots, sizes, setbacks, and build ing 
 envelopes.  
 
2. A letter from ADOT  granting access from SR 260, shall be provided with the Tentative 
 Plat process to the Navajo County. 
 
3. A permanent cross access easement agreement shall be provided from the Bigler’s property on the 
 North, to FS 332 with the Tentative Plat application. 
 
4. The identified secondary access point for the subdivision on the North , which is a segment of 
 Forest Service R oad 332, shall be safe and accessible year -round.  Prior to receiving the first 
 certificate of occupancy, the developer shall improve the existing road segment and provide an all-
 weather surface acceptable to the US Forest Service and Navajo County.  
 
5. Navajo County Engineering and Flood Control requirements shall be met.  
 
6. The number of lots shall not exceed 100 with proven adequate water and sewer systems provided 
 to the lots. 
 
7. A Tentative Plat shall be submitted within twelve (12) months to the Navajo County Planning 
Zoning Department. If a Tentative Plat is not submitted within twelve (12) months to the Navajo 
County Planning Zoning Department, the Special Development (SD) zoning designation of the 
subject property shall automatically revert bac k to the previous zoning classification of the 
property, which zoning designation was placed upon the property prior to the property being 
classified as Special Development (SD).

RESOLUTION NO.  XX-20 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF 
SUPERVISORS DENYING A ZONE CHANGE WITH A  
MASTER DEVELOPMENT SITE PLAN FOR HIGH PINES 
ESTATESIN THE ARIPINE AREA  
 
 WHEREAS, an application was duly filed on October 9, 2019 by High Pines Estates 
 LLC to permit a Master Development Site Plan called “High Pines Estates”; and 
 
 WHEREAS, the application concerns the following real property in Navajo County: 
 APN: 208-03-002A and 208-03-002B, which are portions of Township 11 North, Range 
 18 East, Sections 3 and 9 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian in the Aripine area; and 
 
 WHEREAS, a Public Hearing, as required by Section 2902(2) of the Navajo County 
 Zoning Ordinance, was duly noticed and held on June 4, 2020; and 
 
 WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, after considering the testimony 
 and other evidence presented at the hearing, as well as the recommendations of staff, finds 
 that the Zone Change with a Master Development Site Plan is consistent with the public 
 health, safety and general welfare and should be approved subject to the conditions set  
 forth herein; and 
 
 NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED  the Board of Supervisors hereby 
 deny the rezone with a master development site plan. 
 
 
PASSED AND ADOPTED by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors by a vote of   
______ yeas and ______ nays on this 7th day of July 2020.    
  
 
 By: _______________________________  
 Jason E. Whiting, Chairman of the Board 
  
ATTEST: 
 
 
________________________________ 
Melissa W. Buckley, Clerk of the Board

<!-- page 709 -->
RESOLUTION NO.  XX-20 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF 
SUPERVISORS APPROVING A ZONE CHANGE WITH A  
MASTER DEVELOPMENT SITE PLAN FOR “HIGH PINES 
ESTATES” IN THE ARIPINE AREA  
 
 WHEREAS, an application was duly filed on October 9, 2019 by High Pines Estates 
 LLC to permit a Master Development Site Plan called “High Pines Estates”; and 
 
 WHEREAS, the application concerns the following real property in Navajo County: 
 APN: 208-03-002A and 208-03-002B, which are portions of Township 11 North, Range 
 18 East, Sections 3 and 9 of the Gila and Salt River Meridian in the Aripine area; and 
 
 WHEREAS, a Public Hearing, as required by Section 2902(2) of the Navajo County 
 Zoning Ordinance, was duly noticed and held on June 4, 2020; and 
 
 WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, after considering the testimony 
 and other evidence presented at the hearing, as well as the recommendations of staff, finds 
 that the Zone Change with a Master Development Site Plan is consistent with the public 
 health, safety and general welfare and should be approved subject to the conditions set  
 forth herein; and 
 
 NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED  the Board of Supervisors hereby 
 approves the rezone with a master development site plan,  subject to the following 
 conditions: 
 
1. The lot configurations shall be detailed in Tentative Plat with lots, sizes, setbacks, and 
building  envelopes.  
 
2. A letter from ADOT granting access from SR 260, shall be provided with the Tentative 
Plat process to the Navajo County. 
 
3. A permanent cross access easement agreement shall be provided from the Bigler’s 
property on the North, to FS 332 with the Tentative Plat application. 
 
4. The identified secondary access point for the subdivision on the North, which is a 
segment of Forest Service Road 332 , shall be safe and accessible year -round.  Prior to 
receiving the first certificate of occupancy, the developer shall improve the existing road 
segment and provide an all-weather surface acceptable to the US Forest Service and Navajo 
County.  
 
5. Navajo County Engineering and Flood Control requirements shall be met.

<!-- page 710 -->
6. The number of lots shall not exceed 100 with proven adequate water and sewer systems 
provided  to the lots. 
7. A Tentative Plat shall be submitted within twelve (12) months to the Navajo County 
Planning Zoning Department. If a Tentative Plat is not submitted within twelve (12) 
months to the Navajo County Planning Zoning Department, the Special Development (SD) 
zoning designation of the subject property shall automatically revert back to the previo us 
zoning classification of the property, which zoning designation was placed upon the 
property prior to the property being classified as Special Development (SD). 
 
 
 
PASSED AND ADOPTED by the Navajo County Board of Supervisors by a vote of   
______ yeas and ______ nays on this 7th day of July 2020.    
  
 
 By: _______________________________  
 Jason E. Whiting, Chairman of the Board 
  
ATTEST: 
 
 
________________________________ 
Melissa W. Buckley, Clerk of the Board

Motion before the Board:
EXECUTIVE SESSION pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.03(A)(3) for the Board to receive legal
advice from its attorney regarding the One Arizona Opioid Settlement Memorandum of
Understanding.

litigation.

counsel.

Background:
See confidential attachments.
Recommendation: 
The County Attorney's Office received this proposal on 6/30/20 with a deadline response of July
10, 2020.  We have not had the time to study the proposal or consult with outside legal counsel
prior to the deadline for the submission of agenda items for the July 7, 2020 BOS meeting.   As
such, at the time this matter is submitted, the County Attorney's Office has no recommendation.  It
is anticipated that the County Attorney and outside counsel may have a recommendation by the
time of the Board meeting.
